utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-06-90-T, the Prosecutor versus Ante Gotovina, et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Today, again, the Chamber will sit under Rule 15 bis. I announced on Friday that the absence of Judge Gwaunza would be of a short duration. She expects to be recovered by tomorrow. We'll continue as we did last Friday. The remaining Judges consider it in the interests of justice to continue to hear the case. If there are no procedural matters -- one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We need approximately one minute for the Registrar to verify a certain matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May the witness be brought into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Balunovic. Before you give evidence, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require that you make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing butt truth. The text is now handed out to you by Madam Usher, and I would like to invite to you make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Balunovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, the Chamber was informed that you do not seek any protective measures; and, therefore, you will testify in open court. Mr. Balunovic, could you, first of all, state your name and place and date of birth for the record.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Branko Balunovic. I was born in 1970, in the Republic of Croatia, in Davor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, could you state your rank and could you tell us to what unit you belonged in August 1995.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: In August of 1995, I was in the anti-terrorist unit of Lucko as instructor for specialist training.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us your unit? What operation or operations it was involved in the second half of August 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: In the second half of August 1995, following Operation Storm, my unit participated in clean-up operations in the area around Grubori and Ramljane.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you remember what day the operation in Grubori took place?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think it was on the 25th of August, 1995; at the time when the so-called freedom train was expected to travel along the line. Our task was to clear up a patch of the terrain surrounding the railway line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was your role during this operation on the 25th of August?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: On the 25th of August, I was one of the leaders in the area that was to be cleared up by my unit. There were four of us holding that particular role, and I was one of the four leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you equal among the other group leaders, or did you have any additional task?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: In terms of hierarchy, the four of us were equal. I didn't have any additional task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, could you briefly tell us what your group encountered and experienced during this operation on the 25th of August.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: We proceeded from the starting line as designated, in terms of the area that was to be mopped up. My group was second on the left-hand side, next to Stjepan Zinic's group who was to my left. To my right was that of Mr. Drljo, and to the far right was the group of Mr. Krajina. These are the names of the leaders who were there together with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, once you proceeded from the starting line, what then happened?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Soon after heading from the starting line, in a hamlet of several homes, as far as I remember, my group came across two persons, so it seems to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And what did you do with those two persons?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: The two were elderly civilians. Mr. Jurendic came upon them. He is one of my colleagues. He radioed this information to Mr. Celic, who was in charge of the unit's operation for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Jurendic -- what was his first name; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Ante.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was he in your group?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think he was in my group, because he happened to be in the area that was searched by my group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the Chamber received reports about these events, and we'll come to that at a later stage. But in the -- in two of the reports of group leaders, Mr. Ante Jurendic is mentioned as belonging to that group. Are you aware of Mr. Jurendic functioning in not just your group but also in another group.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. However, since people were not specifically assigned to specific leaders before we set out on the task, it is possible that during the search operation some individuals crossed from the territory covered by one leader to that of another, and, as a result, the names of these individuals may appear in more than one of the reports produced by leaders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, once the two civilians were radioed, or at least the information about them was radioed to Mr. Celic, what then was done, in relation to those two elderly civilians?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jurendic inquired of Mr. Celic of the radio as to what was to be done with these persons, with these civilians. I can't quote his precise words but he said that they should remain there and that somebody would be coming to collect them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you then move on, or did you wait until they were collected?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think I moved on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then describe what you further encountered and experienced when you had moved on?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: We moved ahead from that hamlet. I only recall that the terrain was quite difficult to negotiate at points and we could not maintain the formation that is normally designated for such mop-up operations but, rather, had to change the -- from the skirmish line into a column, a single file.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you -- do you remember any incidents, further during the day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: When we reached the village of Grubori, which was along the axis to be searched by Mr. Drljo, somebody passed on the information over the radio that there was some problems there. At that point, my group stopped there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Up till that moment, as you said, when you reached the village of Grubori, did you hear or see anything beyond the usual?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say that I heard or saw anything that would be out of the ordinary, for that period of time. I can tell you that gun-shots and explosions could be heard from time to time. Given the lie of the land, it was very difficult for me to say where the sound was coming from. I have to tell you that at that time, and it was a time of war, people would open fire even in situations where they would be approaching an area that seemed suspicious. In order to provoke a reaction from such a location, they would fire several bullets in the direction, in that particular direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, once you had heard gun-shots and explosions and when you received information on the radio, what -- how did you respond, how did you react to that information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Let me first clarify one point: The gun-shots and explosions, I didn't mean to say that they happened at a time when we had radio communication. I only wanted to say that during the search operation one could hear gun-fire and explosions which I could not pin-point the direction of. When my unit was searching the terrain, there were several other units both to our left and to our right, who did their searches in their respective areas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps I should more precisely ask you whether once you had moved on, once you had contacted Mr. Celic about the two civilians, was there any radio contact after that, in relation to gun-fire you may have heard?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, there were no further radio contacts. I have to emphasise the fact that radio communications were quite poor at that time in this particular area. The repeaters normally used by the radio communications were dysfunctional, and we oftentimes lost contact with other groups, both visually and in radio communication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, we could have a look at it in further deal if you wish, but in an interview which you've given in 2004 to the Office of the Prosecution, you stated then that when you heard what you thought was rifle fire and when listening to the radio that you heard some communication between other group leaders. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have that on our screen. And let me just check. That is 65 ter 7548. First part, pages 132 and 133.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, we have some technical problems. Let see whether I can ... it might take me a short moment to get the exact text. I'll move on for this very moment, Mr. Balunovic, and we might come back to that at a later stage. Could you please continue? You said you don't remember any further radio communication. What then happened? So you heard some gun-fire; you heard some explosions. What next happened?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: At the moment when we heard on the radio that they had problems in that village, I was somewhere around that village, and one might even say that I kept under my control the area left to the village, which means that I provided security for that area left to the village, and I stopped in that place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say, "in that place," do you mean next to the village, to the left of it; or did you mean to say in the village?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I meant by the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, that gun-fire, those explosions you heard, were they -- how often did you hear that? Was it frequent; was it sporadic; was it constant?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: It was sporadic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What weapons did your unit and your group have at its disposal during that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: We had short-barrelled weapons, pistol, and long-barrelled weapon, rifles. We probably had hand-grenades, but I'm not sure, and I also believe that there were people who had Zoljas or hand-held rocket-launchers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say people had Zoljas, to whom are you referring? Members of your group; member of the other groups? Any specific persons.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't give you any names. And I meant in general terms that it was possible that either in my group or in some other groups, men might have had the type of weapons that I've just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you just told us that you heard fire. You said it was sporadic. Did you at any time notice that you were fired at?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't notice that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apart from what you heard, did you see anything which is worth mentioning?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that I saw anything at that moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say, "at that moment." Was there, at any later stage, something you saw which may be relevant?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At what distance were you approximately from the Grubori village or hamlet?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you precisely. But I believe that the distance was something between 50 and 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see any smoke or any fire?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also not at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I don't remember having seen anything, even at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, are you aware of any prisoners taken during that operation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when did your group meet or merge with members of the other groups?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that that was in the area beyond that village. But I can't say that I saw all the groups that were involved. Above the village, there is a plateau, and I remember that I was waiting there until some of my men came and that, from there, we moved forward. I don't remember having seen anybody from any of the other groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When did you -- when was the whole unit reunited, if they were?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that that happened at the line of -- where our operations ended and that was by a railway track. I would also like to mention that not all of us arrived at the same time. I believe that I was the first to arrive there and that we waited for the others to gather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you were at the railway line, how did you then move on?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: We got into our vehicles there. I am not sure whether the vehicles were already there or whether we had to wait for them. In any case, that was the end of that operation. That's where we got into our vehicles and were taken from there by the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you have to walk along the railway line in order to get you to your vehicles? Did you see any railway stations or ... did you move north; did you move south?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I only remember that there was a little stream separating us from the railway track. There were no bridges, so we will to cross that stream, in order to climb to the railway track. I believe there was a railway station there, but I'm not sure of that. I'm -- I think that there was. And if I remember well, the vehicles were standing there, in that spot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did the vehicles get there? Had the drivers stayed with the vehicles or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, the vehicles deposited us at the beginning of our operation, at the line where our operation started. They took some other way to get to the line where operations -- operation ended. I don't know when the vehicles left from that first line and when they arrived at the last line. I can't remember, or perhaps I didn't even know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the start of the operation, where you got off the vehicles, who had told you where the operation would start? How did you know where to start?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how that transpired. I believe that that was immediately as we got out of the vehicles. If I remember properly, we were transported along a very narrow asphalt road, and I believe that the launch line was right there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And how many were you in a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly, but I can assume that, since the vehicles had seven or eight seats, I believe that the vehicles were full, that there were seven or eight people in the vehicles. It is also possible that some of the vehicles were not full to the capacity, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, were you the only group leader in your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember, did you have maps where to go; or did the driver know; or had someone told you where to go?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that we had maps, but I don't remember at what point we had received them. I believe that it was at the launch line, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Who had briefed you on the operation of that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Celic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where did he brief you, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can only assume that that was either at the launch line or perhaps in Gracac. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, at the end of the operation, did you report to anyone about what had -- what you had accounted during that operation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I reported back to Mr. Celic. I informed him that there had been no incidents on my axis, save for the incident when we found those two civilians. But he already knew that. He had already been briefed on and that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that is what you learned from -- oh, you mean the two civilians earlier?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I mean the two civilians that Mr. Jurendic found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you report anything on the gun-fire you had heard?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't think so. I didn't -- didn't tell him anything about that. But as I've told you, it was not a thing to report about. It was not unusual. You could hear shots and gun-fire all over the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, where did you go after the operation was finished?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that I fell asleep in the car as soon as we started driving, and when I woke up, we were in Gracac. So I would say that after the end of the operation, we returned to Gracac. That was our base -- temporary base in the field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you remember who were with you in your vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember - and I'm sure that Mr. Celic was in the car - he was the driver actually. I'm not sure about the others. I can't remember who else was in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And when you said you orally reported to Mr. Celic, was that in the car; or was that before you boarded vehicle?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe it was before we got into the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But after you arrived at where the vehicles were; is that ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: After the end of the operation, I believe that I reported to Mr. Celic as soon as I saw him. I told him what had transpired on my axis, and after that verbal report, we boarded the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you notice that whether any of the group leaders similarly reported, as I understand, orally, to Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be sure of that. I assume so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And why do you assume so?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, because that was a custom and a normal thing after every operation. The first thing we did after every operation was to brief the operation leader orally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Had any members of your group used their fire-arms during that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that in the field, after the village, as I've already told you, there was an elevation, a plateau. Mr. Garic fired a shot in the direction of a wooden log cabin in that elevation. As I've already told you, it was not unusual for men to open fire or fire a -- a -- a round or two when they thought that they were looking at something suspicious. They simply wanted to provoke an answer from that side, if there was, indeed, something suspicious going on there. Mr. Garic fired - I don't know how many rounds he fired - and I told him that that was enough, that he should no longer open fire, and after that, he did not open fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Garic fired at -- in a direction of a wooden log cabin. Did he hit that cabin; or did he shoot above it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I really can't tell you whether he fired those shots into the cabin, or above it, or by it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did it trigger any fire in return?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, there was no return fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart, perhaps, from being hit by a bullet, did the cabin suffer any further damage, as a result?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, there was none.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it didn't catch fire or was, in any other way, affected visibly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, no such thing happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Later that day, you said you fell asleep in the car. You arrived at Gracac. Did you, at any later point in time during that day, speak with Mr. Celic about the operation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But I would say that we did not discuss the operation any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Also not with members of other groups?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. I don't think that I discussed the matter with anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember at what time, approximately, the operation finished, at what time, approximately, you arrived at your cars?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I really can't remember. Either the launch time or the time when we arrived at the last line. I only remember that it was raining at the end of the operation. There was a thunder-storm going on. It had been raining also during our mop-up operation. But I'm really not sure about any of the times. I can't talk about the times of day, when things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, during the following day, the 26th, did you, during that following day, at any time, discuss the Grubori operation with Mr. Celic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. As far as I can remember, I don't think so. I don't think we did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, as far as the reporting by Mr. Celic is concerned, do you have any knowledge on -- as to how Mr. Celic compiled his report, a report on the events of the 25th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. I have no knowledge about the way he compiled his report. That was above my hierarchical level, and I was really not interested in that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, we have some technical problems. Normally we'd show you on the screen exactly the -- what we'd like to show to you, but I now have to find it and then read it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Balunovic, I would like to take you to the next day; that is, the 26th. And I think you earlier told us that there were operations in Grubori and in the Ramljane area. Was it on the 26th that you were involved in an operation in the Ramljane area?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was involved in an operation in the Ramljane area, and, as on the previous day, I had the role of a group leader.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was the unit divided in four groups, as it was the day before?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: My memory of these events is quite vague compared to Grubori. I think the unit was divided into several groups, but I'm not sure how many.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember to work closely together with any of the other group leaders on that 26th of August?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you depart from Zagreb -- from Gracac that morning of the 26th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I'm not sure. What I remember of the events of that day is that, soon after leaving the starting line, there was fire. Somebody opened fire, and we noticed two uniformed individuals ahead of us. I think somebody said that they were shooting at us and people fired back at them. I think that both of them fled. The next thing I remember, as having happened on the day, is that we were heading along a road for which we had information that it had been mined. I was at the head of the column, and Mr. Neven Juricic [phoen], who was a trained explosives specialist was there with me, we headed the column, as we trod carefully along the road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you shot at? That means, your group.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't claim that with any certainty. But I do recall individuals shouting that we were being shot at, though I don't remember seeing that, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you or members of your group return any fire?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that, at that point, the whole unit was together. That we had not dispersed at that time yet. And I recall seeing, for myself, these uniformed individuals ahead of us. What I don't remember is who opened fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean whether they opened fire, or whether you or members of your group opened fire; is that what you mean to say?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What, apart from this fire, did you hear or did you see?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember anything else from that section of the terrain, from that particular action. My memory of that operation is quite faded. I do recall what happened next, when General Markac came to see us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there for a moment. Did you see any smoke or fire?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that, from the operation's staff, somebody called me over the radio and asked me what sort of smoke could be seen there where I was. I said that I didn't see any smoke and that I didn't believe that it happened along my axis. I don't remember seeing any smoke even later on, though I suppose there was smoke, since Mr. Markac came to see us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why do you suppose that there was smoke when he came to see you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so, because this is an issue that was already discussed in this case, when I had an interview with the ICTY investigators. And also because I believe that Mr. Markac came to see us precisely with the intention of finding out where the smoke came from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you have any explanation, then, as to how he was aware of the smoke and you didn't see it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I have no knowledge of it. I'm saying that I don't remember that smoke, not now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you exclude for the possibility that you have seen such smoke but that you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Is possible that I saw it and that I don't remember it anymore.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier you told the Chamber that someone called you over the radio and asked what sort of smoke could be seen, that you said that you didn't see any smoke.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the point when I was still in the village, because I do remember that there were houses about. I remember him asking me what sort of smoke this was, and I remember answering that I didn't know, because it probably wasn't along my axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember the name of that village?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that you met Mr. Markac. Could you tell us when and where that encounter took place.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that it happened when the operation in Ramljane was over. What I don't remember is the location where it took place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you say, "When the operation in Ramljane was over," how do I have -- were you all together at the target point; or were you on your way back; or -- how do I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I am not sure -- or let me first tell you that I believed the operation was over when we reached the finish line, as it were, and when the unit gathered. I'm not sure if Mr. Markac was already there waiting for us, or told us to wait where we were for him to arrive, or whether he came upon us in a vehicle. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when you saw Mr. Markac, what then happened?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Mr. Markac had a map with him. He wanted to establish what had happened in that section of the terrain and where each of the respective leaders were, which part of the terrain they covered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you give the information he was asking for?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I recall Mr. Celic being there; of course, because he was in command of the unit on the day. If I remember correctly, Mr. Markac asked him about who had passed along that axis through the village. I think that Mr. Celic mentioned me and Mr. Drljo. However, the conversation was interrupted by Mr. Drljo's intervention which was not soldierly, or honourable in any way. If I remember correctly, he started swearing and the oaths were intended for Mr. Markac. He said that he had set alight everything, whatever he could or whatever he wanted. I'm trying to give you the general outline of what the conversation or what the course of these events was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Markac asked about who had passed along that axis through the village. Was there any specific issue he raised in this context?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Earlier you said something about smoke and where Mr. Markac was apparently aware of. Was that, at this moment in time, that he referred to that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if Mr. Markac was aware of the smoke, but I believe that that was the reason why he came to see us, i.e., to establish where the smoke had come from and how this had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And why do you believe that that was the reason why he came to see you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know which other reason he could have had. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did you become aware of smoke which could be seen or had been seen.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question is the following: If you say, The smoke was the reason why Mr. Markac came to see you, this could be explained by either that you had seen that smoke - you said you did not - or that Mr. Markac had seen that smoke, or that it was reported to Mr. Markac that there had been smoke. So I'm just trying to explore why you linked the presence of Mr. Markac with smoke.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I heard, later on, that this apparently had happened at the time of the passage of the freedom train. The freedom train was carrying representatives of the Croatian elite, and, allegedly, some of the passengers of the train intervened and informed Mr. Markac of this. This is hearsay, I'm telling you, that I came to learn later on. I don't know if the events happened this way, really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What triggered Mr. Drljo's comments that he had set everything on fire? I mean, if you're talking about an operation and someone starts talking about having set something on fire, what triggered that; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you this with certainty. I presume, and my presumption is based on my knowledge of Mr. Drljo and his participation in the homeland war, I suppose that the very fact that Mr. Markac came to see us provoked him, triggered this reaction. From Mr. Markac's demeanour, one could infer that something went array. His approach in addressing the unit was such that it seemed that he -- he was already blaming someone, and I suppose that this conduct on the part of Mr. Markac provoked Mr. Drljo and triggered his reaction. Though I have to tell you that this is how I see it. I'm not sure that that is, indeed, the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, I'm looking at a statement you have given in Croatia on the 16th of December. And under normal circumstances, we would show it to you, but I'll then slowly read what you are reported to have said. And let me just see to who you gave that statement. That was a statement you -- it was a witness interview where an investigating judge, Mr. Ivancic, was present. Do you remember having given such a statement on the 16th of December?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I remember giving a statement before Judge Ivancic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I will slowly read the relevant portion.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interprets would kindly request the President to indicate the precise passage he is reading from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm reading from the third page of the 16th of December interview, which we cannot show, unfortunately, on the screen. A line starting -- perhaps we could put it on the ELMO, that's -- but we have no B/C/S ... I see that we have at least a Croatian version on our screen at this moment. That seems to be the document. If I -- now the problem is, that in B/C/S, it is the -- let me try to find it. Could we move on a bit? I think we -- could we move back one page in B/C/S. Could we enlarge it a bit. I will try to find where it is in the original. Yes, it is about -- at a certain moment we have the number 20 metres, and then a couple of lines further down, where the name of Mr. Markac appears. Can you see it on your screen? And I will slowly then read: "I am not sure" -- no. I see "nisam siguran," which sounds familiar to me now: "I'm not sure whether we drove before that or we were about to climb into vehicles when General Markac arrived and asked who set the houses on fire. I do not remember whether he mentioned a name of a village, but it seems to me that he referred to that village we passed through on the second day of the operation." You then continue: "As far as I remember, Franjo Drljo then angrily answered General Markac that he had set those houses on fire." Now, this statement suggests that Mr. Markac specifically referred to houses that had been set on fire. I earlier asked you what triggered Mr. Drljo's response, and you said: "I heard later on that this apparently had happened at the time when -- of the passage of the freedom train." And you say, "This is hearsay." In your statement, we find clearly that you say Mr. Markac asked about who set houses on fire. Now, which of the two is the truth: Did Mr. Markac specifically mention houses being on fire; or is it only that you heard and that you supposed or assumed later on that this is what had triggered his presence and that was part of his questions?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Actually, I don't know, and I'm not really clear on what the dilemma is. I stand by what I said on the 16th of December. I said a moment ago that Mr. Markac's demeanour was such that it clearly indicated to us that one of us had done -- or some of had done something that was clearly not permitted and that was how he approached the entire unit. I can't be sure or quote the exact words of anyone there. But Mr. Markac's demeanour and what was said was roughly along the lines of what I stated on the 16th of December. As far as I remember, Mr. Markac --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. On the 16th of December, you clearly stated - at least that is how it is reported - that Mr. Markac asked about the fire, about the houses being set on fire. [Microphone not activated] ... is that the truth?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe so, yes. I believe that that was the case. But I'm not sure how Mr. Markac had been informed about houses having been set on fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, whether you know that or not, that's not the question, how he knew. But I asked you - and I repeat my question - you said that Mr. Markac asked about what had passed along that axis through the village. And I asked you: "Was there any specific issue he raised in this context." And you said: "I don't know. I don't remember." From your statement of last December, one, it is difficult to understand it in any other way than to say that he raised the issue of houses being set on fire. That's what you apparently said and -- is that what you say is, first of all, what you said in December; and whether that's the truth?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that it happened just the way I described it, on the 16th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I encourage you to directly answer the questions, because it took me quite a while to explore with you what seems to be a relatively simple answer. Now, so we had Mr. Markac raising the issue of houses being set on fire, Mr. Drljo responding to that. Was Mr. Markac calm; was he upset; was he -- what was his -- what could you see? Because you earlier referred to the -- to his behaviour?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If I remember it properly, Mr. Markac was upset, and he was also angry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What then, after this anger being expressed, Mr. Drljo telling that he had set everything on fire, that he set the houses on fire, what then happened? Were any decisions taken? How did Mr. Markac then respond to that situation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: The only thing that can I remember is that after the event, we were sent to Zagreb -- actually, we were first transferred to Gracac to pick up the rest of our equipment. That's where our temporary base was. After that, we were sent to Zagreb, either on the same day or the day after, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you leave for Zagreb that same day or the day after?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. That I believe that was on the same day. But I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when you saw Mr. Markac, who was there present with him, if anyone? I think you already mentioned Mr. Celic. Anyone else?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, I believe Mr. Janic was there. And perhaps Mr. Sacic, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The return to Zagreb, was that already scheduled in advance; or was it decided on that moment?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the arrangements that were made at a higher hierarchical level. That was not part of my job. However, after the passage of the freedom train, there was no longer any reason for us -- for or presence there. I suppose that there hadn't been any other operations planned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Had the freedom train already passed through that area when you saw Mr. Markac?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no direct knowledge of that. But I -- as I have just told you, rumours had it that while the freedom train was passing through, somebody noticed that smoke and informed Mr. Markac. So I would be inclined to believe that the freedom train had already passed when we were sent to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember what time it was that you returned to Gracac?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not even approximately? Like midday or late in the evening or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember. I wouldn't want to misinform you, and I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, it's time to take a break. We have a break of close to half an hour, and we'll resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, we have to try to overcome our technical problems. I hope it goes better. But it causes me to take you back for a while to the first day of the operations, 25th. Could we have 65 ter 7548, page 132, 133 on our screen. At the bottom of this page, Mr. Balunovic, you are talking about the communications. And we now move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, most likely we'll see it on our screen soon. I'll start slowly to read to you, even if we can't see it yet. It is about the events on the 25th of August, and after having been asked about the weather conditions, the following question is put to you: "Okay. And, having heard this shooting, did you go on your radio, or did you receive a radio message?" And then your answer was: "As it was an open channel, I heard Mr. Zinic contacting either Mr. Krajina or Mr. Drljo, one of them, asking what is going on. And as far as I can recall, the response was that they had encountered Chetniks or something like that." Do you remember having stated this in 2004? And I literally read to you what was recorded.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can say that I do not recall the instance when I stated that. It was six years ago, and my recollection of the events was much better then than it is now, so I would be inclined to believe that my statement given six years ago is accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to know the reference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What we have -- great problems here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: I have a hard copy with me if Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if you have a hard copy, I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: On the bottom it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, on the bottom it always says which page out of how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, there, I think it is page 132, 133 of 162 of --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I may assist, Your Honour, it is page 137 in e-court right now of 65 ter 7548, and what Your Honour has read was from line 17 on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, there may be some area of confusion with what Mr. Kuzmanovic has because what was initially disclosed is a different pagination then what is in e-court, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The problem is that two parts of the 2004 statements are put together, which mean that the e-court pagination does not, is the not same --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, as a matter of fact, that is one problem and also there was a revision to the translation and there may have been different versions. The version in e-court now, the final translation, has 167 pages at the bottom. The portion that Your Honour has just read is in page 137 of the version in e-court on the screen right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have it on our screen now, that's clear. Mr. Balunovic, you can read it there what your answer was, can you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you say this -- since it was closer to the events, this may well be the accurate description of what happened. Now, there is one other detail from that statement which I'd like to discuss with you. In that statement, you said something about searching houses as a standard procedure. Was it standard procedure that, if you would see any houses that you would just briefly go into them, in order to find out who is in there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we certainly had to search the houses in the area that we were supposed to search. It would have been impossible to search everything else without making sure that there's no danger coming from the houses, that the houses were safe in the search area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I have to understand it, that if, on your axis, you would see a hamlet or a village that you would, at least, look into the houses in order to see who were present there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I would like to take you back to the 26th of August; that is, the Ramljane operation. Did you report on that on what happened on that day?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I believe so. That report was presented to me in the proceedings conducted in Croatia about a month ago. Before that, I hadn't been even sure whether I had ever written a report about the event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was it usual that you would present a written report on your operations?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in the special police for a number of years. I can say that I joined the moment it was established and continued working after the war for ten years. I can say that the procedure changed, so I cannot be sure that, during the war, we were duty-bound to submit written report about every operation or whether we did it only upon the superior's orders. It is possible that, at that particular time, a verbal report was all that was necessary, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, do you remember who ordered you, if such an order was given, to write a report on the 26th of August?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember when and where you wrote that report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't have any recollection, either of the time or the place where that report was written. As I just told you, it was only a month ago that I learned and was absolutely sure that the report had been written and that it exists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we look at that report; P770. Is that your handwriting, Mr. Balunovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'd like to pay some attention to some details of your report. You write that the report -- that -- that the -- that the terrain search operation took place between 0930 and 1400 hours. Does this, in any way, refresh your recollection?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that operation, but I can't remember the time when it took place. As I already told you, I really have a very vague recollection of that operation. But I do remember that I took part in it, and I do remember what my role in it was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, this report also states that you came under fire and that you returned fire with infantry weapons and anti-tank weapons, which resulted in several buildings and haystacks catching fire. That is not consistent with your testimony of today. Do you have an explanation for that? Because, today, you said that you didn't see any smoke and nothing at all. Here, however, you do report that, as a result of returning fire, several buildings and haystacks caught fire. Do you have any explanation for this inconsistency?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As I have told you, I have a very vague recollection of the details of that operation. I said that there were fires; I don't know how they happened. It is possible that I wrote my report based on assumptions, as to how the houses caught fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now you say: "I said that there were fires; I don't know how they happened." Is that what you said today?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, when I said "fire," I meant rifle fire. I didn't mean burning, houses burning, or anything else burning. "Fire" is a word that we use both for something burning as well as opening fire from weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you also write a report on the events of the 25th?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did write a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember when and where you wrote that report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm quite confused about the -- where that report was compiled. I believe that I wrote it in the base, in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In Zagreb. We'll come back to that at a later stage. I take you back to the 26th. There was this conversation between Mr. Markac and Mr. Drljo, as I understand, an unpleasant conversation. What did you do next? You returned to where?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I believe that we returned to Gracac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then, did you stay in Gracac? Did you ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether we set out for Zagreb on the following day or on the same day. In other words, I'm not sure as to how much time we actually spent in Gracac after the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you, at any time, return to the Grubori area, after you had concluded your operation in the Ramljane area?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I don't know how many days later. I believe that that was maybe a day or two days after the operation in Ramljane. I returned to the area of Grubori, together with Mr. Celic, upon Mr. Sacic's order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, did you then go from Gracac to Grubori; or did you return from Zagreb to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Celic and I were sent back to Grubori from Zagreb. Or, rather, not to Grubori but to the area down there. I remember that I was also in Knin, but I don't remember whether we went to Grubori first and then to Knin, or the other way around. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber has received evidence that you were in Grubori on the 27th of August, together with, among other people, Mr. Sacic. Now, did you go back to Grubori once, or did you go there several times?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that I was there only once.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- would you exclude for the possibility that you stayed overnight in Gracac on the 26th of August and then went to Grubori in the course of the 27th of August?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that we returned to Grubori and that we had spent the previous night in Zagreb; I'm sure of that. In other words, we spent one night in Zagreb and then we were dispatched to Grubori. I believe -- or, rather, I'm sure that we arrived in Grubori from Zagreb and not from Gracac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Do you remember at what time approximately you arrived Grubori on the day you were there?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you see when you returned to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: The scene that I saw in Grubori still haunts me and still affects me whenever I have to talk about it. We entered the village, and the first thing I noticed was a lot of carcasses of animals, pigs or perhaps cows. I'm not sure about the cows, but I remember the pigs. At the entrance to the village, we were met by a civilian, by a gentleman. I suppose that he was one of the locals. And when Mr. Sacic saw the dead pigs lying about, he asked the gentleman, What was that? And the gentleman answered something to the effect, Well, the pigs are the least of the damage. The biggest damage are the dead people. And then he started taking us from one a place to the next where the bodies of dead people lie.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You saw the bodies of the dead people?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Celic with you when you saw the dead people?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Sacic with you when you -- when you saw the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain that he was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you told before going there why you would go to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if I was told specifically why we were going there. I think that we were generally told that there were some problems down there and that that was the reason why we had to return.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What kind of problems?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall the words that were used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But what was the gist of it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: In fact, I didn't know what it could possibly involve. I think that the situation as it existed out in the field was different from how Mr. Celic reported on it, and that was the reason why we had to head down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you told what the difference was?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall it being told to me that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apart from Mr. Celic and Mr. Sacic, who else were present when you came to Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember seeing Mr. Cermak; that's to say, in Grubori. But I don't recall at which point this was. In fact, I remember that we were at Mr. Cermak's in Knin, but I'm not sure if we went to Grubori first and then to Knin. I think that we were, in fact, first attending the meeting in Knin and then headed for Grubori, where we were joined by Mr. Cermak. Though, again, I'm not sure of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you return to Knin after you had been in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I remember that I was in Knin, attending a meeting of sorts with quite a few persons in attendance, but I don't recall any other details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You told us that Mr. Celic was there; Mr. Sacic were there; that, either at that moment or at any other point in time, you saw Mr. Cermak. Was Mr. Turkalj in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was Mr. Markac in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Markac was not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when you saw these dead bodies, what then happened? Was this discussed or -- what was said about it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that this person took us to the various spots where dead people lay in Grubori. I myself didn't go everywhere. I recall that Mr. Sacic, although I do have a confusion in my head on this score, I remember that there was an old man, his dead body, that is, in a house. He a wound on his neck. There was a woman there, mourning and lamenting his death. I recall her telling us, Look how they cut his throat and pointing to his neck with his finger. And I recall Mr. Sacic saying that this wasn't a knife wound, rather, the exit wound of a bullet which had entered the neck from the back, from the nape. I recall that there was somebody taking a photograph, although I can't tell you whether this was part of general crime scene examination or not. I also don't remember where we headed next, after visiting Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, how many dead bodies did you see?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Just one matter of translation while we're here. It's been pointed out to me by a language speaker that at 37, 6, a different phrase was used from the word "general" and it might be a phrase that's familiar to Your Honour from these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we then perhaps -- for me, it's 37, line 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: A term of science rather than art.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I can't tell you," you are translated to have said, "whether this was part of ..." Part of what exactly? Could you answer the question, Mr. Balunovic? I'm just asking to you repeat your answer in that respect because there may be a translation issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think if you would read from the beginning of the sentence until you read, that might give the witness a better context of what ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Starting at "I recall"? Yes. Mr. Balunovic, I read from what appears on our transcript: "I recall that there was somebody taking a photograph, although I can't tell you whether this was ..." And then what did you then say? I think I started saying: "... by part of ..." Part of what?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I wasn't sure whether the taking of photographs was part of an on-site investigation or crime scene examination in order to establish facts, or whether this was -- this had some other purpose, the taking of photographs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What other purpose could that have been?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. For the media perhaps. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you see any investigating judge? Was there anyone with you, who you thought or knew was an investigating judge?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think that there were members of the uniformed police with us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were there any members of the crime police? To say not special police but crime -- the policemen which would normally investigate a crime scene.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you this with any degree of certainty. At the time, the police was not distinguishable by their uniform. You couldn't tell by their uniform whether it was a crime investigation police or any other branch of police. So I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you notice anything in the behaviour, in the active of the policemen present that they were involved in a crime scene investigation?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, only the taking of photographs could indicate this sort of activity. I don't remember observing any other sort of activities. I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you spontaneously came up with the possibility that it would have been for the media. What made you -- what made you think that it could have been for the media?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, you asked me what other purpose the taking of photographs would have, and that's the only thing that occurred to me at the moment. That's why I said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any media present?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any cameras, video cameras, of a profession kind?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember. Let me note that I was quite shocked by everything I saw there, and perhaps my ability to observe matters was a bit impaired by what I experienced there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before Mr. Kay sought to have a translation issue resolved, I asked you how many dead bodies you had seen. Could you tell us how many you saw?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I said already that I saw the old man. I saw another dead body in a house that was burned. The body was burned too. I recall a limb missing on the body, but I don't remember if it was an arm or a leg. There was another body lying in a house, but I didn't want to enter any more houses. I also saw two more bodies, lying in a meadow. I watched them from a distance. So I saw the total of four bodies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And during this whole visit, was Mr. Sacic always there next to you; or was he -- or did he leave; or did he ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I think that I was with Mr. Sacic up until the point when we saw the dead body of an old man in a house. As I said, I didn't want to enter any other houses; whereas, Mr. Sacic proceeded to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So when you saw the bodies in the meadow from a distance, was Mr. Sacic with you at the time, looking from a distance, or did he come closer to the dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, after you had been to Grubori, or before, as you were not certain about that, you said you had been in Knin. Where were you in Knin, and with whom?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said that I wasn't sure what followed after we came from Zagreb. We first reached Gracac from Zagreb, and then, together with Mr. Sacic, we proceeded. Now, whether we proceeded first to Knin and then to Grubori, or vice versa, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question was where you had been; or were you just driving through; or did you stop? Did you have -- did you meet anyone, did you ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If you mean Grubori, we walked through Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I meant Knin.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I remember, we reached Knin in vehicles, of course. The next thing I remember was this meeting, of sorts, in Knin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What meeting was that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't really know what the specific -- specific purpose of the meeting was. I remember Mr. Sacic and Mr. Cermak attending the meeting. I remember persons wearing uniforms of the general duty police, ordinary police, I suppose, that they were there as participants in the meeting. As for the meeting itself, I remember next to nothing. I think that there was discussion of the need to carry out a crime scene investigation and the sanitisation of the terrain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us some more details about that discussion. Who said what? What was the sequence to be followed? Crime scene investigation first and then sanitisation? Or could you tell us the gist of that conversation.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot give you the details. What I would like to point out is that I didn't feel that I belonged at the meeting, because these were high-ranking individuals, and I wasn't, in fact, interested in such meetings. I was even annoyed by them. I thought that I was out of place there, and that I would feel much better being elsewhere. I recall a loud discussion, Mr. Sacic shouting, but I'm not sure what the substance of this conversation or discussion was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now -- Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. President, this is very unusual for me, but I have actually noticed a translation issue as well. At page 41, line 9, and the reason I notice it is because it was the same word that had happened before, it was page 41, line 9. And it is a term that is now very familiar to me in the B/C/S original as well. So if we could seek the same clarification again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When you earlier told us, Mr. Balunovic, that you think that there was a discussion of the need to carry out, did you refer to an on-site crime investigation and the sanitisation of the terrain? Is that what you referred to?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on-site or crime scene investigation and sanitisation, or what is meant by it is the burial of the dead.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. Sacic shouting. Was it about the same subject on what had to be done; or was it, rather, about what had happened; or could you try to see what you remember?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, allow me to say that I could answer most of the questions by saying that I am not sure, and it -- it applies to this question as well. I am not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, this Chamber has heard evidence that, in the context of the Grubori events, that there have been at least two type of discussions. The one was about what to do: On-site crime scene investigation; or not, just sanitisation. Another subject on which the Chamber received evidence, as a matter that was discussed, was how to explain the events. Was it the result of combat or armed resistance and how this may have been caused. As far as the discussion with Mr. Sacic -- or Mr. Sacic shouting is concerned, does any of these two possible subjects - and again, the Chamber received evidence on discussion about these matters in this context - does that refresh your memory in any way?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Again, I wouldn't want to venture into unknown territory. I, perhaps, wasn't even present at the meeting throughout the time. Maybe I went out of the room, since, given the hierarchy of the participants at the meeting, I didn't feel that I was where I should be, that my place was there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you -- had you reported already at that time on the events or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If you mean my report, I don't think I wrote it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, before we come to your report being written, did you ever discuss with Mr. Celic how he reported about the events?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember if I discussed this with him or not. I know that later on his report did not reflect the situation in the field and that he wrote another report subsequently.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And did you -- did he tell you on the basis of what he wrote that second report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He told me that he wrote the second report based on instructions from Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he tell you when he wrote that report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember him telling me that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you remember were you present when that report, based on Mr. Sacic's, his instructions, was produced?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I recall a situation where Mr. Celic and I were in Gracac. I don't remember when this happened, in relation to the other -- other events we are discussing here. I do remember that I stayed behind in either the kitchen or the corridor of the building where the special police HQ was housed and that Mr. Celic went to a meeting with Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said this in answer to my question when that report was produced. What made you believe that that meeting was the meeting where Mr. Celic produced his report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying this on the basis of what Mr. Celic told me at a later date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what you saw, Mr. Sacic and Mr. Celic going to a meeting. Do you remember whether other persons went there as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If I remember correctly, I was received by Mr. Pucek [phoen] I believe, who offered me food; or was it Mr. Cvetko [phoen], I'm not sure. Now I don't know who else may have participated in the meeting, if anyone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you were in the corridor or in the kitchen. Where were these, Mr. Pucek or, perhaps, Mr. Cvetko. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Pucek, that was his name. I'm not sure if I saw one of them or both of them. I only know that one of them offered food, and I remained either in the corridor or in the kitchen eating; whereas, Mr. Celic went to a meeting with Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You saw them together entering a room or did you -- what did you see exactly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. I can't say that I saw them entering that room together. But I believe that I have been told to wait there because he was supposed to meet with Mr. Sacic, or attend a meeting with Mr. Sacic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Balunovic, did you ever see that report that was, at that occasion, produced by Mr. Celic. Did you ever see it at -- in this period of time, so not whether you saw it at a later stage, but whether you saw it in late August or September 1995.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me then turn to your report, in relation to the events on the 25th of August. You said you think that you wrote that report in Zagreb. Could you tell us about the circumstances: Who asked you to write the report; when was it; where did you write it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I remember that we had a meeting in our base in Zagreb. And I believe that the meeting took place in Mr. Turkalj's office. He was the unit commander. And we were told that written reports had to be compiled about the events in Grubori. I believe that a written order had arrived to that effect from the command of the special police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who had called for that meeting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I believe that it was Mr. Turkalj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Recently, you gave a statement to the Croatian police. I think you said that Mr. Celic had called the meeting. But could we have a look at 65 ter 7540, page 3, both in B/C/S and English. Do you remember giving a statement on the 1st of October, 2009, Mr. Balunovic? Approximately a half a year ago.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember either the occasion or -- or when that happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It says that Josip Celic called a co-ordination meeting and invited the commanders of all the combat groups. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I just wanted to place on the record the Court is aware of our position on the issue of Official Notes. So I just wanted to ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes that's -- yes, that's ... You see that, you are reported to have said that the meeting was called by Mr. Celic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: It is possible. I don't know who called it. Maybe we should clarify one thing. Calling a meeting does not mean to be in charge and have the main say at such a meeting. I can't remember. I don't know. It is possible that Mr. Celic informed us to show up for the meeting, and that may have been the case, especially if I said so in my statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What then happened during that meeting? Who addressed you; who said what had to be done, if anything?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If I remember things well, I believe that Mr. Celic told us that Mr. Sacic had provided him with some information that should form the base of a report to be compiled about the events in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Were you aware of that information? Did you know what ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I was aware of all that information beforehand. Since I was in Gracac together with Mr. Celic, he may have told me something about all that even before the meeting, but I cannot be sure of that. I can't confirm that with 100 per cent certainty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you meet with him the day before the meeting? Or before the meeting? Did you discuss the events in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember whether we discussed that. We worked together. He was my superior. We must have seen each other. We must have spoken. But I really can't tell you, and I can't be sure whether a topic of our conversation was also Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, can we have a look at your -- first of all, did you write it down by hand, or how -- and where did you write the report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, usually we wrote our reports in handwriting -- handwriting, and then somebody would copy them on a computer. It would be either the secretary or a desk officer in the unit. I believe that I compiled my report in the meeting room, not in the room where that particular meeting was held, but another room that was used for the service or by the service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So did you do that immediately after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I can't tell you whether it was immediately thereafter, but I believe that we had been given a dead-line. I'm not sure whether that was immediately after the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at P572. Could we go to the second page in the original. Mr. Balunovic, do you recognise your signature under it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is not my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Balunovic, when you had written this report, was it given to you to -- when it was typed out, was it then given to you for reviewing it?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. If I had reviewed it, I suppose that it would now bear my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
