utterances.text: Yes. When you got it typed out, and irrespective of the signature at this moment, did you make any comments and did you say, It's right, or it's wrong, or it should be different?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I have already told you, I believe that I never saw this report typed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You've never seen a typed-out report on the events of the 25th August?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know that there are two reports. Two reports were written on my behalf depicting that event. One of them does bear my signature and the other one doesn't. And -- and the two reports differ in one part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, my question to you is whether you looked at the typed-out report and whether you -- forget about what you see on the screen, forget about your signature at this moment. I want to know how it had happened. It has happened, I should say.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm confused. I don't know want to say. What I see before me is a typed-out report and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, no, I asked you not to look at what you see. Can we get it off our screens. What I want to know is: You made a handwritten report. What then happened?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what happened, but it was common practice to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: -- refer our report to somebody who would type it out, on a computer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you do so?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe so. It would have been following the customary procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My question is whether you remember to whom you gave it.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It could have been one of the two people in our unit. I apologise, I misspoke. Three persons were able to type the report out, but I could have also given that report to my superiors who would have then made sure that it was typed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So did you then see the typed-out report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: The one that I signed, I believe that I did. But I don't recall that particular moment, when I saw it and when I signed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, when you received the typed-out report, did you comment on it? Did you make any corrections? Or did you change it in any way? Or was it exactly as you expected it to be?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that there were any changes. I believe that Mr. Celic requested for an addition to be made to the report, that I should state that before we launched the operation that we had been warned about the treatment of the civilians, and that he also made sure that we knew that we were supposed to abide by the international humanitarian laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said he requested for an addition. So, therefore, an addition to the report you had submitted initially?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, possibly. Yes. I -- it was possibly the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, when I asked you whether any corrections were made, apparently this was added to the report. Was this added once you had seen the typed-out report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know at what point in time was that thing added. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And how was it added? Did you add it to your handwritten report or -- and did you phrase the lines yourself or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. But I believe that I did it myself, that I was the one who composed those sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, as far as the phrasing of the report is concerned, where did you get the information which you -- which you did write down in your report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: If my memory serves me well, the information was conveyed to us by Mr. Celic at that meeting, in Mr. Turkalj's office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. How was it conveyed to you? In writing or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember how it was conveyed. I believe that while I was writing my report, I did have something on a piece of paper. I would assume that those were the guide-lines that I drafted myself, while Mr. Celic was telling us about the information that our reports should contain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, in your -- in the Official Note of your interview which was taken on the -- was held on the 1st of October, you said that you received a piece of paper and that you based your report on that.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That also could have been the case. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, do you remember whether the other group leaders, how they received their information?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that all of us group leaders attended that meeting and that they heard the same information I did, and that they were conveyed the same information I was conveyed. But I don't know -- I don't know how that information was conveyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the -- 65 ter 7540, page 3 in both versions. Could we move a bit down in the English. You are reported there to have said that: "At the meeting, Celic told the participants exactly what to write in their reports," and that you're almost certain that "each participant received the instructions on a piece of paper on which they based their reports." And then it continues that you stated that you acted according to Celic's order, that is -- And could we move to the next page in English. And that you didn't ask any questions. That is what you are reported to have said during your interview on the 1st of October. Does this refresh your memory in any way?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. As I have already told you, I'm not sure how the information was conveyed. In other words, I don't know whether the information was already written on paper and distributed, or whether I made my own notes during Mr. Celic's presentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, as far as the report is concerned -- and let's move to P573. And could we move to the second page in B/C/S. Is that your signature, Mr. Balunovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: This is my signature, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, in this report, events are described in a way which are quite different what from you testified that you observed on the 25th. Did you have any hesitation to write it down, in accordance with the information that was given to you?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hesitate. This report consists partly of what I saw in the field and partly of the information that we received from Mr. Celic. At that point in time, I didn't know what had actually happened in Grubori, and it was not unusual to base our reports not only on our direction knowledge but also on the information obtained from different sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your report, you described that Mr. Stevan Granovic [phoen] was arrested. I earlier asked you whether any -- whether it was your -- whether you were aware of any arrest made that day. You said no, you were not. Now someone else tells you that someone was taken prisoner, and you just write it down for the truth of it without knowing whether it was true?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as for somebody having been arrested and what their name was, we heard that from Mr. Celic, and he supposedly had heard that from Mr. Sacic. As I already told you, I did not have the control over the entire mop-up area so I really don't know what happened. And, actually, I could not refuse to put in my report what my superiors -- superior told me had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why couldn't you refuse?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was no reason for me to doubt his words. I did not have a -- any reason to not to believe that something had happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Celic being present during the operation in Grubori?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Celic remained at the starting position, at the launch line, and I believe that he took over those men that were found by Mr. Jurendic. The next time I saw Mr. Celic was at the final line. In other words, he was not with us during the mop-up operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, we will have a break, and we will resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, a few more questions about your report and the person taken prisoner. All the groups of the units ended up in the same place, and you told us that you had not seen any prisoner being taken. What this Chamber does not fully understand is that you apparently take it for granted that someone was taken prisoner, if you never saw any prisoner at the point where you gathered at the end of the operation.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, as I said, not all of us reached the end line at the same time, nor do I remember a meeting taking place. I think that each of the group leaders submitted their own report to Mr. Celic. So it could have happened that I didn't notice it, that I didn't observe it, and that someone was taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, during this meeting where you were invited to write the report, or instructed to write a report, was Mr. Drljo present as well?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Drljo was present, but he left the meeting, if I remember correctly, and said that he would not be writing a report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did he say why he did not want to write a report?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember him explaining anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you sure about this; or do you say, Well, I just don't remember.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I don't remember him explaining anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look at 65 ter 7540, page 6 in the English; 4 in B/C/S. Could we -- one second. I just have it on my left screen and not ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, I'll withdraw the question in relation to this interview. I would like to take you back to the -- to your signature. You are sure that the one document without the additional line does not bear your signature; is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Balunovic, I have looked at the other report. And perhaps we could show, first, the signature under P572. Second page. Second page, the original. Now, you say this is certainly not your signature.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am pretty sure it's not mine. I don't think I ever signed my name this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we have a look --

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Besides, whenever I sign with my first and last name, I would always first write my first name and then my last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And -- now, are you aware of -- has this ever been investigated by -- Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Maybe we can ask the witness if he knows the -- what the letters next to his name typed out are. My understanding is that they may have some significance in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether I fully understand you, Mr. -- but that may be my -- "v.r.," what does "v.r." stand for?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That could mean, I believe, personally, in one's own hand. In other words, once my name was typed up, this means that I personally sign in my own hand what was written above. That's what the abbreviation stands for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that doesn't appear on the other one, does it? Could we have look at the other -- 573, I think it is. Yes. Yes, now, do you usually sign just with -- without a first name? Or what's the -- what are you usually doing when signing a document?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Initially, I would sign both with my first and last name, and as of late, I only sign my last name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in 1995?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. But I believe that, by that time, I had already been signing only with my last name, unless I was required to do otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we have a look at P770. That's your handwriting and your signature, Mr. Balunovic?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do you know whether this has ever been further investigated on -- whether the version with or the version without the extra line, whether the signatures were false? Under the one or under the other.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask, has it ever been investigated by anyone?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I don't think so, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't think so. Then let's move on, Mr. Balunovic. Only a few more questions. Apart from what you knew at the time, did you receive any further information about the Grubori incident in the years that followed?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in fact, this wasn't much talked about among people. And I think it was in 2003 that I learned a bit more about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you learn about it, and how?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: A very good friend of mine came to see me in my office at the base. At the time, I was assistant commander of the unit. I think it was at the time when the ICTY investigators started interviewing us in Croatia. He came to my office and told me that he was in that group in Grubori, that he had seen quite a lot, and that he would not allow Mr. Celic or I to suffer something that we were not responsible for, and that, when the time came, he would testify about the things that he saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Who was that good friend of yours?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That was Mr. Igor Radocaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, did you ever receive an information from a person named Marijan Sosa.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's right. Marijan Sosa also told me something about these events. Also after 2002 or 2003, I'm not sure. He also told me that Mr. Drljo had threatened him. Apparently, at one point, he called him to get into a car with him, that he had just recently bought in order to show him how good the car was. Marijan allegedly refused at first but then he managed to persuade him to get into the car. Marijan then told me that Drljo drove him to the Stupnik forest, which is close our base, the base of the anti-terrorist unit of Lucko. I can't quote his exact words, but he told me that he had threatened him along these line, that if he said anything about the Grubori case that he would bury him in the woods so that nobody would find him, something to that effect. Marijan said that he had been trying to get out of the car, as the other one was telling him this, but that the doors were locked by an automatic lock. Marijan tried to get out, but then, in the end, he --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure which of the two drew out a pistol and threatened him with, I don't remember which words.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Marijan also told me that on one other occasion, as I was getting out of Lucko base compound in my car, I saw Marijan and Drljo speaking at the gate. Marijan later on told me that on that occasion, Drljo told me, and I apologise for the term I'm going to use, that that asshole also needed to be settled or done with. In other words, he was referring to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now did Mr. Sosa tell you about what knowledge he had of the events or what he heard about the events?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I didn't make a -- either a mental or a written note of it, of the things that he said. He did say quite a few things, and I can't either quote him or tell you with certainty which were the words that he used. Still, his story boiled down to the following: He saw that Drljo and Igor Beneta had killed somebody in Grubori.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say he saw. Did he see that with his own eyes or ...

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Marijan Sosa told me that he had seen it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: He was in one of the four groups?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, what you just told us is in line with what you said on the 16th of December of last year, when you were interviewed. Now, in a later interview - 25th of February of this year - you denied to have had any contact with Mr. Sosa. Could you explain what made you change your mind between last December and February? If you'd like to have a look at it, we'll have a look at 65 ter 7650. Page 4 in English; page 3 in B/C/S. Do you remember that you gave different accounts of your communication with -- Three in B/C/S; 4 in English.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know how to explain this situation to you, other than by saying that I have been experiencing psychological problems, and that the situation is aggravating my condition. That second time when I was giving my statement, I simply couldn't remember what it was that I said in my first statement. And, in fact, I don't agree that I -- that I said that I hadn't had any contacts with Marijan Sosa and that he hadn't told me anything. I don't know how this found its way into the document. In other words, I stand by what I told you a moment ago. The only dilemma and uncertainty I have in this regard has to do with what they told me about who it was that Drljo had killed and who it was that Igor Beneta had killed. As I said, unfortunately, I didn't feel the need, at the time, to make a note or try and memorise these conversations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you stand by your testimony given today, that Sosa, as an eye-witness, told you what he had seen.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have no further questions for you at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, we have 15 minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you wish me to start?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it's -- perhaps I inform the parties that, of course, all the travelling arrangements that were scheduled for today didn't work out and, therefore, it is very unlikely that we would have our next witness here by tomorrow even the day after tomorrow. It is highly uncertain when aviation will start again. The Chamber has in mind to deal with some procedural matters if we would have any time left today, but let's first hear the testimony of the witness in cross-examination. Mr. Balunovic, you'll now be cross-examined by Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Hedaraly is counsel for the Prosecution, and you will find him to your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Balunovic.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can we first have 65 ter 7660 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And it will come up on your screen in a few seconds. And that will be the decision of the Ministry of Interior to appoint you as an inspector of the Lucko Anti-Terrorist Unit as of the 1st of May, 1995. And when you see that on the screen, can you please confirm that that, in fact, was your position in 1995. Just take a few seconds. We still have some technical difficulties, but I think they are almost resolved.

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would only like to say the following: The interpretation said inspector and I wasn't an inspector. I was an instructor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, on the English translation of the document, it says the position of specialised training instructor, and the title is inspector, first-class or inspector; perhaps that's the confusion. Is that accurate, what you see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, instructor of specialised training was an occupation post, which required the rank of an inspector. So such decisions always designated the post that was to be occupied as well as the police title required.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me just show you a second document which is related.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And that's 65 ter 7661.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: This is the next decision concerning you and the Ministry of Interior. That one is dated 1 January 1996. And there it says that you are still a specialised training instructor, so that specific position the title is of independent sergeant. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if you go to the bottom of that page, the last paragraph in the English starts: "Given that the civil servant named does not meet the conditions necessary for the appointment into the title prescribed for the civil servant position under item 1," and we can turn the page in English, "of this decision but that it is estimated that he will successfully discharge the duties of the said civil servants position ..." And then it goes on. Have I understood correctly that as of 1 January 1996, you received a position for which you were not yet qualified but for which you were expected to become qualified? Have I understood this document correctly?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that you were promoted as of 1 January 1996 and that you were expected to fulfil the requirements of the qualifications of the new position at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell now, because I don't see that the decision mentions any sort of qualifications. It is noteworthy that the Law on Internal Affairs was amended and the whole structure of the police changed over time, so perhaps this was due to certain administrative reasons that called for the issuing of a new decision that would be in accordance with the regulations in force at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, were you promoted as of 1st January 1996 or did your functions changed [sic] in any significant way?

utterances.speaker: BRANKO BALUNOVIC
utterances.text: No. The post remained the same, that of the specialised training instructor. In other words, both the 1995 and 1996 decisions regulated the same posts and the same type of duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I have 65 ter 7660 and 65 ter 7661 admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 7660 shall be assigned Exhibit P2724. 65 ter document 7661 shall be assigned Exhibit P2725. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P2724 and P2725 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will be moving into another topic, and I can start, but I will not be finished in ten minutes; but I leave it up to the Chamber's discretion, if you wish me to start now and complete tomorrow, or take an early break or deal with other matters and start -- continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we give up time, could you give us an estimate on how much -- perhaps we -- Yes, do you understand, Mr. Balunovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it's not a secret anyhow. Could you give us an estimate, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will need one -- one to two sessions. Hopefully closer to one than to two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as of now, one session at the maximum.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: At the moment, no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think it's better that we adjourn for the day. Mr. Balunovic, we'll continue tomorrow. We'll finish for today. I would like to instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether it is testimony you have given already today or whether that is still testimony still to be given tomorrow. So not to speak or, in any other way, communicate with anyone about your testimony. Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KUZMANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, after the witness is excused, I just wanted to talk about a logistical thing, as long as we have a few minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we have. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00, Mr. Balunovic. You are excused. You may follow the usher. But only for the day.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kuzmanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Move into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. We'll adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, the 20th of April, 9.00 in the morning, this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 20th day of April, 2010, at 9.00 a.m. 21 22 23 24 25
